claim: Every kilogram of the 100 kg input leaves as products (32.3), flake (19.3), metals, e-waste, paper or disposal (28.4)
law: Conservation of mass (RFE-CAL-001 section 2)

claim: In water, PP and HDPE flake floats and PET and PVC sink, so float-sink separates them (it cannot split HDPE from PP, which are sorted into their own bins at the table)
law: Archimedes: a flake floats if its density is below water's (1.00 g/cm3); HDPE 0.94 to 0.97, PP 0.90 to 0.91, PET 1.33 to 1.45, PVC 1.38 to 1.41 g/cm3 (KiTech; recipes)

claim: The hot sheet press loses about 0.8 kW standing when hot
law: Conduction through 50 mm mineral wool (k 0.045 W/m K) over the platen packs at 175 K, plus 50 % for edges and frame; closed press only (losses while loading and through the frame and jacks not counted)
closed_by: Open: measure the standing loss on the built press (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: At full heater power the 5 kW press puts a 12 mm HDPE sheet's heat in within the published 55 min cycle (cooling is in the separate cooling press)
law: Energy balance: sheet and mould heat 2.56 kWh (HDPE cp 2.25 kJ/kg K over 175 K plus 180 kJ/kg fusion, about 62 % of the 293 J/g of fully crystalline PE) at 5.0 kW less the 0.8 kW standing loss; average draw over the cycle 3.6 kW

claim: Heat reaches the middle of a 12 mm sheet well inside the 55 min cycle
law: Transient conduction t = L^2 / alpha (alpha 0.21 mm2/s for HDPE), x1.5 for the latent heat, x4 for a loose flake bed

claim: HDPE and PP are processed at 190 to 210 C, below the 230 C (HDPE) and 240 C (PP) ceilings of their processing ranges
law: Processing ranges HDPE 190 to 230 C, PP 200 to 240 C (RJC Mold chart; Precious Plastic Extrusion Pro)

claim: PVC is never heated: it releases hydrogen chloride at press temperatures, and float-sink cannot remove it from PET
law: PVC dehydrochlorination: 0.4 mol % HCl lost in 30 min at 200 C (Szarka and Ivan, 2013); PVC 1.38 to 1.41 g/cm3 sinks with PET
check: Exclusion rule at sorting (safety rules, recipes, BLD stop S6); within known chemistry

claim: PET is sold as flake, not melted: it must be dried to about 0.005 % moisture at 150 to 175 C for 4 to 5 h or it hydrolyses in the melt
law: Hydrolytic degradation of PET in the melt (Plastics Technology, How to Dry PET)
check: Design choice decided by Amish, 2026-09-25 (RFE-DDR-001 item 3); consistent with the chemistry

claim: Polyolefin melt fumes contain formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, acrolein, CO and a wax aerosol, so every melt process needs local exhaust
law: Borealis, Statement on impurities: polyolefins, ed. 6, 2022
check: Two enclosing hoods, G4 and F7 filters, impregnated carbon, stack above the roof (RFE-CAL-001 section 6)

claim: The press booth's extract (0.5 m/s at the sash) carries away the hot-platen plume, so fume does not spill out of the sash
law: Axisymmetric plume mass flow m = 0.071 Qc^(1/3) z^(5/3) + 0.0018 Qc (NFPA 92, a fire-plume equation used here as a heuristic well below its range), Qc from natural convection off the open 1.1 m platen, z to the booth roof; a hot mould being unloaded is a larger, short source

claim: The 250 mm duct runs at a transport velocity that keeps the wax aerosol from settling
law: Duct design velocity: ACGIH gives about 5 to 10 m/s for vapours and fumes; 10 m/s is used here so the condensed wax aerosol does not settle (design choice, both hoods drawing)

claim: The 1.5 kW fan moves 0.57 m3/s against 815 Pa with dirty filters
law: Fan input = Q dp / (fan 0.55 x motor 0.85)

claim: The line uses 1.0 kWh or less per kilogram of output with motor and drive losses counted (was 0.83 on shaft power)
law: Electrical energy = shaft energy / (motor x drive); IE3 minimum efficiencies, IEC 60034-30-1 (ABB note): 2.2 kW 86.7 %, 1.5 kW 85.3 %; drive 96 %; single-phase pump 75 %
closed_by: RFE-DEC-001 D2 (fix made 2026-10-25: CAL counts motor and drive losses)

claim: The block A loads run on a 230 V, 40 A single-phase supply (the old figure was 8.75 kW = 38.0 A at unity power factor)
law: I = P / (V x PF x eta); drive input currents from datasheets (Schneider ATV12: 20.2 A at 2.2 kW, 14.9 A at 1.5 kW, 240 V); single-phase motor currents NEC Table 430.248
check: Block A 55.4 A running (72.0 A at full load; arithmetic sum of table currents, a conservative upper estimate) against 40 A; block B 36.4 A, 91 % of the supply as a continuous load. Fixes: three-phase 400 V supply (18.5 A per phase if balanced) or three time blocks on single phase (largest 36.4 A, about 10.6 h day, about 13 USD a shift more in wages)
closed_by: Open: RFE-DEC-001 D1, proposed, awaiting Amish

claim: With the lined enclosure the shredder operator's 8 h exposure is 85 dB(A) or less (sound power assumed 102 dB(A))
law: Lp = Lw + 10 log(Q / 4 pi r^2 + 4 / R) in the reverberant steel room; 15 dB insertion loss; LEX over 3.79 h
closed_by: Open: measure the machine's sound power and the enclosure on site (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: A 15 dB insertion loss is possible with the feed slot open
law: Open-area limit on insertion loss IL <= 10 log(S_enclosure / S_open)

claim: A hand through the feed slot cannot reach the cutters: the slot is 120 mm high (ISO 13857 Table 4 range) and the path is 1,060 mm against 850 mm
law: ISO 13857 Table 4: slot 40 < e <= 120 mm, safety distance 850 mm; above 120 mm the reaching-over distances apply (Troax and Axelent guides to ISO 13857)
closed_by: Open: fix D3 made 2026-10-25 (slot 160 to 120 mm); the EN 12012 type C standard for size reduction machines, which takes precedence over ISO 13857, still to check; cutter height assumed

claim: A UB 305 x 165 x 40 that fits the reserved 165 x 305 mm space carries the roof edges over the 12 m seam (top flange held by the roof)
law: Bending only: M = w L^2 / 8 at ULS (1.35 g + 1.5 q; roof 0.20 kN/m2 plus 0.40 kN/m beam, imposed 0.75 kN/m2 over 2.44 m) against Wpl fy (623 cm3, S355). Unrestrained it would buckle laterally, so the top flange must be tied to the roof; service deflection about 41 mm (L/290) misses L/360, and racking stiffness lost with the side walls is not checked: both for the structural engineer

claim: The container floor carries the 430 kg hot press
law: Line load on a 40 ft container floor, 3.0 t/m allowed (TIS, ISO 1496 limits); press over 1.2 m

claim: No one lifts more than 25 kg: flake and product lots are packed in 25 kg bags or moved on the transfer bridge
law: ISO 11228-1 reference mass 25 kg is for ideal conditions; frequency, height (the feed lip is at 1.70 m) and reach multipliers reduce it
closed_by: Open: apply the ISO 11228-1 multipliers to the real lifts with the partner; smaller bags if needed

claim: Air at the workstations stays below the occupational exposure limits for formaldehyde and acrolein with the hoods running
law: OSHA PELs: formaldehyde 0.75 ppm (8 h), acrolein 0.1 ppm; emission rates of small open machines are not published
check: Hoods sized for 0.5 m/s; exposure can only be shown by air monitoring on a running site
closed_by: Open: air monitoring on a running site (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Washed flake on 7.2 m2 of trays dries by the next shift with the 0.4 kW fan running through the 8 h shift
law: Psychrometric moisture pick-up: about 0.3 m3/s past the trays at 4 g of water per kg of air, against 30 % water on the day's flake over the 8 h the fan runs (still air overnight not counted)

claim: The shredder's assumed 15 kg/h lies inside the published 8.8 to 41.8 kg/h range for its class
law: Precious Plastic Shredder Pro published range

claim: The extruder's assumed 5 kg/h lies at the low end of the published 5 to 15 kg/h for the Extrusion Pro class
law: Precious Plastic Bazar listing, V4 extrusion: 5 to 15 kg/h at 4 kW, 400 V

claim: Every passport record validates against schema v0.2, and a product lot without parents is rejected
law: JSON Schema draft 2020-12 validation of the example records (RFE-CAL-001 section 11)
check: 3 of 3 examples valid; the negative case is rejected

claim: The site breaks even at a product price of about 2.49 USD/kg (arithmetic only: the inputs, including the 2.50 USD/kg price, are assumptions)
law: Hand recomputation: (all costs per shift including equipment recovery - other sales) / product mass

claim: A lithium cell crushed in the shredder can start a fire, so cells are pulled out at intake and kept in dry sand
law: US EPA, An Analysis of Lithium-ion Battery Fires in Waste Management and Recycling, 2021
check: Intake rule, fire-safe sand container in the cage, BLD stop S5

claim: Option B: a 10 t vertical baler makes bales of about 120 kg of sorted PET bottles
law: Bale mass = chamber volume (1.0 x 0.7 x 0.75 m) x bale density, taken as about 230 kg/m3 to match the supplier listing's 120 kg (so not an independent estimate); platen pressure only about 0.14 MPa
closed_by: Open: bale density on a trial bale (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Option B: a 2.2 kW single-phase power pack drives the 10 t ram at a usable speed
law: Ram speed v = P eta / F (eta 0.7) against a usable minimum of about 10 mm/s (a 1 m stroke in under 2 min)

claim: Option B: the baler, fans and lights run on the 40 A single-phase supply
law: NEC Table 430.248: 3 hp (2.2 kW) single-phase motor 17 A at 230 V; lights 1.7 A; a 0.4 kW fan 4.9 A

claim: Option B: four people sort and bale 300 kg of input in a shift
law: Three sorters at 25 kg/h for 4 h (the rate in RFE-CAL-001) with the fourth weighing, baling and issuing passports

claim: Option B: a 120 kg bale is never lifted by hand; it moves on a pallet truck
law: ISO 11228-1 reference mass 25 kg; bales and pallets on a hand pallet truck
